newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close lower in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close lower in cautious trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended slightly lower on Friday as a late speculative rally in textiles failed to overcome profit-taking in the heavily weighted financial sector, brokers said.
The weighted index ended a scant 9.50 points or 0.14 percent lower at 6,578.36. Turnover was a modest T$47.33 billion.
The market continued a consolidation triggered when the index reached a 19-month high on Saturday.
Financial shares, largely responsible for a recent bull run, suffered from active selling, losing 1.31 percent.

"Some investors wanted to change their holdings today for speculative purposes, and since financials are the most heavily weighted sector it became the selling focus," said George Hou of Jardine Fleming.
Central Insurance dropped T$2 or 3.17 percent to close at T$61, and Kaohsiung Business Bank fell T$1.50 or 2.65 percent to T$55.
Textiles were the main target of speculative buying, gaining 2.51 percent with Shinkong Synthetic Fibre rising 5.91 percent or T$1.40 to T$25.10.

Electronics shares rose 0.91 percent as the sector continued to feed off bullishness from Tuesday's news that semiconductor book-to-bill figures for the United States climbed to a new year high in September.
Shamrock Technology enjoyed a "honeymoon bounce" to soar the daily seven-percent limit or T$2.50 to T$39 on its listing debut. Acer Sertek also ended limit-up, gaining T$3.50 to T$59.
Brokers expected consolidation to continue in the near future, with no signficant factors seen to upset the current balance. A 6,550-6,620 range was seen for Saturday.
